figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the Cephalonauts One dataset. A. Three subjects listened to podcasts during fMRI acquisition. B. Each session included five 15-minute runs, three comprehension questions after each run, and a final anatomical scan. Runs 1–2, 3–4, and 5 used three distinct podcasts and podcasts were not repeated across sessions.

Table 1: Brain datasets using speech stimuli. Maximum hours per subject reports the maximum subject-specific stimulus duration. For LeBel et al. [2023] we report the 2 available data regimes. Benchmark-oriented denotes releases with benchmark tasks, metrics, baselines, and code.

Table 3: Released brain data. We release three versions of the preprocessed fMRI data generated with DeepPrep: native T1w space, MNI space, and the fsaverage5 cortical surface. V denotes the number of voxels or surface vertices.
Table 4: Released stimulus representations. For each stimulus modality, we release both segmentlevel data and embeddings from foundation models. D denotes the embedding dimensionality.

Figure 2: Dataset construction and decoding framework. A. For each frame t, stimulus zt is aligned with fMRI recordings sampled every 520 ms. Target stimulus embeddings yt summarize the audio waveform or transcript over the stimulus context leading up to t. The corresponding brain input uses preprocessed fMRI volumes shifted by a fixed lag. In this illustration, the stimulus context spans 1.56 seconds (3 TRs) and the lag is set to 1.04 seconds (2 TRs). In the experiments, we set the lag to 2.5 seconds and the stimulus context to 10 seconds. B. A pretrained encoder maps stimulus Z to stimulus embeddings Y . The decoder fθ is trained to predict Y from pre-processed brain recordings X .

Figure 3: Speech decoding performance versus training-set size. Test performance is shown versus training hours for each subject, using Median Relative Rank, Top-10@2000, and Cosine Similarity. Lower is better for Median Relative Rank; higher is better for the other metrics. Error bars show one empirical standard deviation across five folds with distinct held-out test sessions. Performance improves with additional subject-specific data, with no clear saturation. Chance level is 0.5 for Median Relative Rank and ∼0.5% for Top-10@2000.
